message.content: {"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report clearly states “GROSS/MICRO FINAL INVASIVE TUMOR SIZE … 3.2 x 3.0 x 3.0 cm,” which exceeds 2 cm and makes the tumor T2. In its reasoning the model applies the correct AJCC size rules but still outputs T1, showing it never incorporated the 3.2 cm measurement; it must have missed or mis-read the key size information rather than mis-applying the staging rules."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size (5.2 cm) and stated the proper AJCC size thresholds (T2 ≤ 5 cm, T3 > 5 cm), but then erroneously concluded that 5.2 cm “is not more than 5 cm.” This faulty numeric comparison led to the wrong T stage assignment."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor dimensions (2.4 × 2.2 × 2.7 cm) but then mistakenly stated that this size is \u001cwithin the T1 range\u001d (< 2 cm). It performed an incorrect numerical comparison (treating > 2 cm as < 2 cm), leading to the wrong T-stage assignment."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model correctly extracted the key facts (13.6 cm tumor, satellite skin nodule, and epidermal involvement) but then asserted that T4 requires skin ulceration or invasion \"beyond the margin.\" That is a misstatement of AJCC rules—any satellite skin nodule or direct invasion of skin qualifies as T4b regardless of margin status. Thus the error stems from applying an incorrect staging rule, not from missing information."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report clearly states a right-breast invasive carcinoma “spanning a distance of 65 mm,” which meets T3 (>5 cm). The model ignored this larger tumor and focused only on the 21 mm left-breast lesion, so it never considered the decisive fact for staging."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor sizes (1.5 cm and 2.2 cm) yet concluded “this falls under T1, as it is less than 2 cm.” It mis-compared the largest focus (2.2 cm > 2 cm) to the AJCC threshold, showing faulty numeric reasoning rather than a misunderstanding of the rule or missed facts."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor sizes (≈3 cm and 2 cm) and noted absence of chest-wall/skin involvement, but it wrongly asserted that axillary lymph-node metastasis (6/10 nodes with extracapsular extension) makes the tumor T4. Lymph-node status defines N stage, not T stage, so the model applied an explicit, erroneous AJCC rule, demonstrating incorrect staging knowledge rather than extraction failure."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly quoted the tumor dimensions (\"5.5 cm … 8 cm … 4.5 cm\") but then claimed the tumor was “not more than 5 cm,” ignoring that 5.5 cm and 8 cm exceed the 5 cm cutoff for T3. It had the right data but applied an incorrect numeric comparison, leading to the wrong T stage."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model extracted the correct tumor size (2.8 cm) and even cited the correct rule that T1c is for tumors >1 cm and <2 cm, yet it still classified 2.8 cm as T1c. The mistake lies in failing to correctly compare the number 2.8 with the 2 cm cutoff, not in extraction or rule knowledge."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model extracted the correct tumor size (2.5 cm) and even stated the correct AJCC rule that T1 is ≤ 2 cm, yet it still assigned T1c. The mistake lies in comparing 2.5 cm to the 2 cm cutoff, a pure quantitative mis-judgment, not a misunderstanding of the rule itself."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model correctly noted the report’s description of skin involvement/inflammatory features, but then stated an incorrect AJCC rule (“tumor of any size with direct extension to the skin” = T3). According to AJCC 7th ed., such skin extension makes it T4, so the error arises from wrong staging knowledge, not from mis-reading the report."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report clearly states that the invasive carcinoma invades the dermis with overlying skin ulceration and explicitly labels the tumor pT4b. The model’s explanation only cites the 7 cm size and ignores these passages, indicating it failed to extract the critical ‘skin ulceration’ information rather than mis-applying staging rules."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted that the tumor measured 7.8 cm (> 5 cm) and noted no chest-wall/skin invasion, but still labeled it T2 instead of T3, indicating a failure in the numerical comparison of tumor size to the AJCC thresholds."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model extracted the correct tumor size (2.6 cm) and stated the correct AJCC rule (T1 ≤ 2 cm). It then incorrectly concluded that 2.6 cm is \u001c≤ 2 cm\u001d and assigned T1c instead of T2, a clear numeric comparison error."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly states \"T Stage: 3,\" but the model ignored this fact and fabricated a tumor size of \"2 cm or less,\" leading it to select T1. The failure lies in extracting/recognizing the provided stage, not in applying rules or arithmetic."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Inference","reason":"The model correctly extracted that the report already states \"T Stage: 2 (T2)\" but then chose to ignore this explicit information and tried to re-derive the stage from tumor size (which is not given). Thus the facts were available, yet the model drew the wrong conclusion by over-riding the stated T2, an inference error rather than an extraction or knowledge error."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly states “T Stage: 2,” but the model ignored this fact and instead hallucinated that the tumor size was “2 cm or less,” leading it to assign T1. The information needed for the correct stage was present; the model simply failed to extract it."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly states “T Stage: 2,” but the model claims the tumor is ≤2 cm and therefore T1. It failed to extract the stated T stage and instead invented an unstated tumor size, so the mistake occurred during information extraction, not inference of AJCC rules."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly states “T Stage: 2”, but the model claimed no tumor-size information was present and output “unknown.” Thus the relevant fact was present but not extracted, leading to the wrong prediction."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly states \"T Stage: 2\", but the model ignored this and instead hallucinated a tumor size \"2 cm or less\", then reasoned from that false extracted fact. The mistake occurred before reasoning—key information was missed/mis-read—so the error is due to incorrect information extraction."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly states \"T Stage: 2\" but the model missed this and instead hallucinated a tumor size \"2 cm or less,\" leading it to choose T1. The mistake occurred before any staging logic was applied, so the core issue is faulty extraction of facts from the text, not incorrect application of AJCC rules."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size (11 cm) but then asserted that lack of chest-wall/skin involvement “rules out T3,” showing it believes T3 requires such involvement. That is an explicit misstatement of AJCC rules (T3 is defined solely by > 5 cm size). Thus the error stems from wrong staging knowledge, not extraction or arithmetic."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model extracted the correct tumor size (3 cm) and correctly stated the AJCC rule that T1 is ≤ 2 cm, but then erroneously concluded that a 3 cm tumor “is still within the T1 category,” showing a faulty numerical comparison rather than a misunderstanding of the rule itself."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size as 2.4 cm, but then erroneously claimed that 2.4 cm is \u001cwithin the range of T1 (≤2 cm)\u001d and specifically T1c (<2 cm). The facts were seen; the mistake was a faulty numeric comparison, not a mis-read fact or wrong AJCC rule statement."}

{"error_cause":"Conflicting Ground Truth","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size (2.7 cm) and applied the standard AJCC 7th-edition rule that tumors > 2 cm and ≤ 5 cm are T2. The pathology text supports this. The provided ground-truth label of T1 (≤ 2 cm) contradicts the report, so the error stems from an incorrect dataset label, not the model’s reasoning or information extraction."}

{"error_cause":"Conflicting Ground Truth","reason":"The model correctly noted skin ulceration/skin involvement, which under AJCC-7 (T4b: tumor of any size with ulceration or direct invasion of skin) makes the case T4. The dataset label of T3 (>5 cm without skin/chest-wall extension) conflicts with these findings, so the error lies in the ground-truth label, not the model’s extraction or inference."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the invasive tumor size as 3.5 × 2 × 2 cm but then mistakenly said this size was “between 1 cm and 2 cm,” classifying it as T1c. This is a mis-comparison of numbers, not a failure to read the report or a misuse of AJCC rules."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model extracted a tumor size of 2.6 cm correctly but stated that this \"falls within the T1 category,\" explicitly applying a wrong AJCC threshold (T1 ≤ 2 cm, T2 > 2 cm ≤ 5 cm). Thus, it saw the relevant fact yet used an incorrect staging rule."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model accurately extracted the tumor size of 3 cm from the report but then mistakenly treated 3 cm as if it were ≤2 cm, assigning T1c. This is a simple mis-comparison of numbers, not a mis-reading of the report or misuse of staging rules."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size (3 cm) and even stated the proper size range for T1c (1–2 cm), but then erroneously concluded that 3 cm fits that range, showing a failure in basic numeric comparison rather than a misunderstanding of AJCC rules."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly states an invasive ductal carcinoma measuring 3 × 2.5 × 1.5 cm (specimen A), which exceeds 2 cm and determines a T2 stage. The model’s reasoning cites only the 1.5 cm residual focus from specimen B and ignores the larger 3 cm measurement, so it failed to extract the key size information, leading to an incorrect (T1c) conclusion."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the invasive tumor size of 2.0 cm but then mistakenly stated that 2.0 cm is “greater than 0.5 cm but less than or equal to 1 cm,” assigning T1b. This is a faulty numerical comparison, not a misunderstanding of the report or AJCC rule wording."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Inference","reason":"The model correctly extracted the key fact (tumor size 8.3 cm) but then mis-applied the staging rules: it acknowledged that T3 is for tumors “more than 5 cm” yet still concluded the size “exceeds the limit for T3” and assigned T4 without evidence of chest-wall/skin invasion. Thus the facts were right; the conclusion was wrong due to faulty reasoning, not faulty extraction or arithmetic."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model correctly pulled the invasive size (2.5 cm) from the report, but in its explanation it states that 2.5 cm “falls within the T1 category” and that T1b applies to tumors “larger than 1 cm but less than 2 cm.” Those statements reveal an explicit, incorrect AJCC rule set. The mistake is therefore due to wrong staging knowledge, not information extraction or simple arithmetic."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Inference","reason":"The model correctly extracted that the largest individual invasive focus is 1.5 cm (≤2 cm) but then mistakenly based staging on the 2.7 cm aggregate size of multifocal tumors. It applied the correct size thresholds (≤2 cm = T1, 2–5 cm = T2) to the wrong measurement, leading to an incorrect T2 conclusion. The facts were seen; the logical application was wrong."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size (4.5 cm) but then mistakenly stated that 4.5 cm is “larger than the 5 cm limit for T2,” leading it to choose T3. The mis-comparison of 4.5 cm versus 5 cm is a numerical error, not an extraction or rule-interpretation issue."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly states “EXTENSIVE DERMAL LYMPHOVASCULAR EXTENSION IDENTIFIED (T4d)” and that the tumor extends into the dermis, both of which qualify for T4 regardless of size. The model’s rationale ignores these statements and bases staging only on tumor size, showing it failed to extract the critical skin-involvement information from the text."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor’s largest dimension as 2.2 cm, but then applied wrong AJCC rules: it claimed tumors >2 cm and ≤3 cm are T1c and that a 2.2 cm tumor does not meet T2 criteria (<5 cm). These explicit, incorrect stage-size thresholds show faulty knowledge of AJCC staging, not an extraction or arithmetic problem."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Inference","reason":"The model correctly extracted the key fact (tumor size 4.0 cm) but then drew the wrong conclusion: it claimed that a tumor > 2 cm “rules out” T2 even though it simultaneously quoted the correct rule (T2 = up to 5 cm). It also mis-interpreted skeletal-muscle involvement as evidence for T3. No facts were missed; the error arose from faulty reasoning, not faulty extraction or an explicitly misstated AJCC rule."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model extracted the correct tumor size (2.0 cm) but then asserted that 2 cm corresponds to T2, explicitly applying an incorrect AJCC rule. This is a knowledge error, not a reading or arithmetic mistake."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report uses commas as decimal points, indicating a tumor measurement of about 1.2 × 1.0 × 1.0 cm, consistent with pT1c. The model mis-read the middle value \"10\" as 10 cm, treating the tumor as much larger, and therefore could not assign T1. The incorrect size extraction, not faulty AJCC logic, caused the error."}

{"error_cause":"Incomplete Information","reason":"The pathology report never specifies the invasive tumor\u0019s greatest dimension; it gives only the overall specimen size. Without an explicit tumor size, the model reasonably concluded the T stage could not be assigned. The ground-truth label of T1 relies on information that is not present in the text, so the error stems from missing detail in the report, not from the model\u0019s extraction or inference."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The model picked the 2.7 cm/2.8 cm macroscopic dimensions and assumed they were the largest invasive focus, ignoring the report’s explicit staging code “pTIc” (T1c) and the possibility that the invasive component is ≤ 2 cm. Thus it had the right AJCC rule but extracted the wrong size datum from the report."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly states \u001cpT4b\u001d and describes skin ulceration/proliferation, which up-stages the tumor to T4. The model only extracted the tumor size and ignored (or did not notice) the skin involvement facts, so the wrong stage came from missing key information, not from misapplying AJCC rules."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report explicitly notes “Infiltratio carcinomatosa cutis et musculi pectoralis,” which makes the tumor T4 (skin and chest-wall involvement). The model focused only on the size measurement and missed these invasion findings, so it extracted the relevant facts incompletely and consequently chose T3."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumour dimensions (1.6 × 1.5 × 1.3 cm and 1.6 × 1.5 × 1.2 cm) but then added the three dimensions together to create a fictitious “size” of 4.4 cm, instead of using the largest single diameter (1.6 cm). This arithmetic misuse led it to classify the case as > 2 cm (T2) rather than ≤ 2 cm (T1). The AJCC rule it cites is correct; the error lies in its numerical handling of the measurements."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor dimensions (3.5 cm) but then stated it was “between 1 cm and 2 cm,” assigning T1c. The wrong size comparison, not a mis-reading of facts or AJCC rule, caused the error."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report clearly states \"invasive ductal carcinoma … measuring 2.2-cm\"; the 0.6 cm figure refers to margin distance, not tumor size. The model treated 0.6 cm as the tumor size, judged this to conflict with the 2.2 cm statement, and declared it unable to stage. Thus it mis-read the key fact (tumor size), not the staging rule, leading to the error."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the largest tumor size (3.5 cm) but then incorrectly concluded that 3.5 cm exceeds 5 cm, leading it to rule out T2 and select T3. The faulty numeric comparison, not a misunderstanding of AJCC rules or data extraction, caused the wrong stage assignment."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Inference","reason":"The model correctly extracted the tumor size (3.2 cm) and even stated that this should correspond to T2 or higher, but it still concluded T1, inventing speculation about mastectomy removal. Thus the facts were available, yet it drew the wrong conclusion."}

{"error_cause":"Numerical Incompetence","reason":"The model correctly extracted the largest tumor dimension (2.2 cm) but then wrongly decided it could “round down” to 2.0 cm, placing the case in T1. This faulty numerical handling (2.2 cm → ≤2 cm) led to the wrong stage despite having the right data."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model accurately extracted the invasive size (2.3 cm) but asserted that a tumor larger than 2 cm still qualifies as T1c, explicitly applying an incorrect AJCC boundary; this is a knowledge error, not an extraction or arithmetic mistake."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Knowledge","reason":"The model extracted the correct tumor size (5.5 cm) but mis-stated the AJCC rules: it claimed that T3 requires BOTH size > 5 cm AND direct extension to chest wall/skin, which is false (size > 5 cm alone is sufficient). This explicit, incorrect rule led it to reject T3 and select T2, so the error stems from faulty staging knowledge rather than data extraction or arithmetic."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report clearly describes a right-breast invasive carcinoma measuring 4 cm (pT2) and a left-breast tumor measuring 1.8 cm (pT1c). The model fixated only on the left-breast size and ignored the 4 cm right-breast tumor, so the relevant fact for staging was missed, leading to the wrong T stage. The inference applied to the extracted fact was correct; the extraction itself was incomplete."}

{"error_cause":"Incorrect Information Extraction","reason":"The report clearly states the invasive tumor measures 3.4 cm (largest dimension). A tumor > 2 cm and ≤ 5 cm should be staged pT2. Because the model output T1 (which requires a tumor ≤ 2 cm), it must have failed to capture this 3.4 cm measurement and instead latched onto some other, smaller number mentioned elsewhere (e.g., 2 cm margin distances, 1.2 cm nipple distance, 0.7 cm lymph node). The staging rule itself is straightforward and widely known; the mistake stems from not extracting the correct tumor size from the text, not from misapplying AJCC criteria."}
